findings.title: Inbound X-Request-ID is trusted verbatim - unbounded length and forgeable value
findings.detail: The caller-supplied X-Request-ID is used with no length cap, no character-set restriction and no format check, then echoed in the response header and written into every log line. Verified live: a 200000-character header was accepted in full, producing a 200146-byte JSON log line and a 200 KB response header (log-flood / storage amplification, and lines above a pipeline's per-event cap are dropped, destroying the audit trail for attacker-chosen requests). A caller can also pick any value, including one shaped exactly like the server's own uuid4().hex, so another request's correlation id can be collided with or impersonated and nothing records that the id was client-supplied. Not a data-exposure or code-execution path, hence WARN.
findings.fix: Honour the inbound header only when it matches a strict pattern such as ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$, otherwise generate a fresh uuid4().hex; when an inbound id is honoured, keep the generated id as request_id and record the caller's value as a separate client_request_id field.

findings.title: Unhandled-exception tracebacks bypass PII redaction and lose the correlation id
findings.detail: RedactionFilter.filter returns early when the _sensitive_values contextvar is empty, and redact_values() resets it in its finally block. An exception raised inside a redact_values scope propagates out of that scope (ServerErrorMiddleware re-raises, CorrelationIdMiddleware resets request_id_var) before uvicorn logs it on uvicorn.error, by which point both contextvars are gone. Verified on a live uvicorn server: a RuntimeError carrying pan=ABCDE1234F and a config path, raised inside redact_values(PAN), was logged with the PAN in cleartext and "request_id": "". The module docstring's claim that the traceback is covered holds only for exceptions the handler catches itself, and the static guard test cannot catch this - a module using redact_values correctly still leaks. WARN rather than BLOCK only because no PII exists anywhere in the tree at HEAD, so there is no reachable path in this diff; it becomes a live PII leak as soon as the first PII-accepting endpoint (E4-S1) merges.
findings.fix: Make redaction independent of the raising scope: either bind sensitive values for the whole request scope in the middleware (cleared after send completes), or catch Exception in CorrelationIdMiddleware around await self.app(...), log it there while the contextvars are still bound, and re-raise. Add a test that raises out of a redact_values block through the real ASGI stack and asserts the value is absent from the captured uvicorn.error record.

findings.title: OpenAPI schema and Swagger/ReDoc UI served unauthenticated with no environment gate
findings.detail: FastAPI(title=settings.service_name) leaves openapi_url, docs_url and redoc_url at their defaults; /openapi.json, /docs and /redoc all answer 200 anonymously (verified). Today only /health is disclosed, so current disclosure is trivial, but this is the app-factory story: every future route, model, field name and error schema is published to anonymous callers automatically, and no Settings flag can turn it off per environment. /docs additionally returns HTML loading Swagger UI from a third-party CDN with no CSP and no subresource integrity.
findings.fix: Add an explicit environment field to Settings and pass openapi_url=None, docs_url=None, redoc_url=None outside development (or require auth on them once authn lands).

findings.title: Error envelope context/detail is an unfiltered outbound channel, and AppError defaults to status 500
findings.detail: The handler serialises exc.context (typed Mapping[str, object], populated freely by any raiser) straight into the response body, and exc.message into detail, with no allowlist, no value filtering and - unlike log output - no RedactionFilter on the path. A future subclass placing a file path, SQL fragment, config value or applicant PAN in context ships it to the caller unchallenged. Nothing internal reaches a client at HEAD (no production code raises AppError yet), hence WARN. AppError.__init__ also defaults status_code=500, so an error raised without an explicit status returns an internal developer-written message in detail on a 500. Secondary robustness note: a non-JSON-serialisable context value (e.g. the Decimal that configured_value naturally is) makes JSONResponse.render raise inside the handler and converts the intended 4xx into a 500. Class-name disclosure via error is judged acceptable - the frozen api-contracts.md mandates it and the names are a deliberate domain error taxonomy.
findings.fix: Restrict context to JSON primitives and have each subclass declare the keys it may publish; suppress detail/context for any 5xx (fixed message, log the specifics instead); make status_code required, or default it to 400 so 500 is never accidental.

findings.title: The two money wire parsers disagree, and both silently round caller-supplied amounts
findings.detail: D-G specifies one wire form (a quoted 2dp string) but neither end validates it; each hands the string to its decimal library. Measured divergences on identical inputs, Python _validate_money vs decimal.js: " 10 " -> 10.00 backend / throws frontend; "0x1f" -> rejected backend / 31.00 frontend ("0b101" -> 5.00, "0o17" -> 15.00); "1E+26" -> rejected backend / accepted frontend; "1_000" -> 1000.00 on both though not contract-legal. Both ends also silently round finer-than-2dp input ("10.005" -> 10.01, "0.999" -> 1.00, "1e-999999999" -> 0.00), so a submitted amount can be accepted at a different value with no error and no audit record. Related files: backend/src/types/money.py:59, frontend/src/types/money.ts:24.
findings.fix: Enforce a canonical form on both sides before parsing - reject anything not matching ^-?(0|[1-9]\d{0,11})\.\d{2}$ (12 integer digits matches NUMERIC(14,2)) with a 422 instead of rounding, and apply the identical check in toQuantizedDecimal. Keep ROUND_HALF_UP for computed values only, never for inbound parsing.

findings.title: Frontend money parser can be driven into heap exhaustion
findings.detail: toQuantizedDecimal calls new Decimal(value).toDecimalPlaces(2) with no magnitude bound. Measured: new Decimal("1e999999999").toDecimalPlaces(2) allocated 4 GB and killed the Node process with FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit after ~16s; in a browser this is a renderer/tab OOM. isFinite() does not help because the value is finite. Reachability at HEAD is low (the string comes from an API response and the backend rejects such magnitudes; no user-input form exists yet), hence WARN; it becomes directly reachable once any form, URL parameter or third-party payload feeds Money.fromWire. Reached from frontend/src/ui/components/MoneyText.tsx:14.
findings.fix: Apply the canonical-format check from SEC-I2-W05 (which bounds both digit count and exponent) before handing the string to decimal.js, and throw InvalidMoneyAmountError otherwise.

findings.title: JS dependency tree is unpinned, and npm audit reports 1 critical / 1 high in the toolchain
findings.detail: (1) package-lock.json is excluded from version control by .gitignore:49 (confirmed with git check-ignore), so no lockfile is tracked: every install re-resolves the ^ ranges, no integrity hashes are pinned, builds are not reproducible and a compromised transitive patch release lands silently. (2) npm audit on the landed manifest reports 5 advisories: critical vitest (arbitrary file read/execute when the Vitest UI server listens), high vite (path traversal in optimized-deps .map handling; NTLMv2 hash disclosure via UNC paths on Windows - this is a Windows dev host), moderate @vitest/mocker, esbuild (any website can issue requests to the dev server and read the response) and vite-node. Installed: vite 5.4.21, vitest 2.1.9, esbuild 0.21.5. All are devDependencies, none ships in a deployed artefact, and the critical one requires vitest --ui which no script starts - hence WARN, not BLOCK. The esbuild/vite advisories remain a live developer-workstation exposure while npm run dev is running. If project policy is 'no critical/high from npm audit at merge', this is the finding that converts to a BLOCK.
findings.fix: Stop ignoring package-lock.json, commit it and install with npm ci; raise the declared ranges to patched majors (vite >= 6.4.3, vitest >= 4.1.11 plus transitive esbuild/vite-node/@vitest/mocker) and re-run npm audit to zero. The .gitignore line is outside this diff, so that edit belongs to its owner.

findings.title: No security response headers on any response
findings.detail: Measured on GET /health, responses carry only date, server, content-length, content-type and x-request-id. No X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, no X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, no Content-Security-Policy, no HSTS, no Cache-Control: no-store. Impact is limited while the API is JSON-only, but the same app serves an HTML page at /docs that pulls third-party CDN scripts with no CSP and is framable, and later groups will return money-bearing JSON that intermediaries should not store. The server: uvicorn banner also advertises the stack.
findings.fix: Add a small ASGI middleware alongside CorrelationIdMiddleware setting X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none', Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and Cache-Control: no-store, and run uvicorn with --no-server-header in deployment.

findings.title: A handled AppError produces no log line at all
findings.detail: The handler returns a response without logging, so the only server-side trace of a rejected request is the truelend.access status line; the error name, message and context are never recorded. For an underwriting decline or policy rejection this is a missing audit record, and it leaves the client as the only party who knows why the request failed.
findings.fix: Log the error (name, status, context) at WARNING/ERROR inside the handler, where the correlation id and redaction scope are both still bound.

findings.title: extra= fields are silently discarded by the formatter
findings.detail: JSONLogFormatter builds its payload from five fixed keys, so logger.info(..., extra={...}) never reaches the sink. This is currently a safety property (PII in extra cannot leak - verified) but it is undocumented and cuts both ways: a developer adding extra={"applicant_id": ...} sees the field vanish with no warning and may conclude the redaction filter handled it.
findings.fix: Document that extra is intentionally dropped, or emit an explicit allowlist of record.__dict__ keys through _scrub so structured fields are both supported and redacted.

findings.title: Redaction remains opt-in, skips short values, and can be bypassed by a late logger
findings.detail: Three residual limits beyond SEC-I2-W02: (a) the static guard test matches only the literal field names pan/aadhaar/salary_doc, so a module naming the same data id_number, uid, payslip or taxId passes the guard while logging it raw; (b) _MIN_REDACTABLE_LENGTH = 6 means any registered value shorter than six characters is never redacted (fine for PAN and Aadhaar, not for an OTP or a 4-digit suffix); (c) _install_redaction_filter_everywhere only walks loggers existing at configure_logging() time, so a library imported later that sets propagate=False with its own handler bypasses both the JSON formatter and the filter - the uvicorn/gunicorn handling is an explicit by-name fix for exactly this shape.
findings.fix: Grow the guard's field-name list from specs/design/CONTEXT.md, lower or remove the length floor for explicitly registered values (anchor the pattern instead to control false positives), and assert at startup that every logger reachable at request time propagates to the JSON handler.

findings.title: Money accepts amounts far outside NUMERIC(14,2)
findings.detail: The only magnitude limit is the 28-digit decimal context, so Money accepts values up to roughly 9.9e25; measured, "999999999999999.99" (15 integer digits) is accepted. D-G stores money as NUMERIC(14,2) (12 integer digits), so anything larger validates here and then fails at the database, turning a caller input error into a 500 rather than a 422.
findings.fix: Enforce the D-G domain bound in Money.__init__ (reject abs(amount) >= 10**12), matching the canonical wire regex in SEC-I2-W05.

findings.title: No environment/hardening flag in Settings, and log_level is unvalidated
findings.detail: No hardcoded secret and no insecure default exist here, but nothing distinguishes a production run from a local one - which is what SEC-I2-W03 (docs endpoints) and SEC-I2-W08 (headers) both need. log_level is a free-form str passed straight to root.setLevel(), so TRUELEND_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG in production silently widens log output and with it PII exposure, while a typo raises at startup.
findings.fix: Add a constrained environment: Literal["local","test","staging","production"] field and make log_level a validated Literal/enum.

findings.title: MoneyText lets a parse failure escape into render
findings.detail: The component accepts money: Money | string and calls Money.fromWire during render, so InvalidMoneyAmountError propagates into React's render phase and, with no error boundary in the tree, unmounts the subtree. One malformed amount in a list of loans blanks the whole view.
findings.fix: Parse at the data-fetch boundary and pass a Money, or render a fallback for an unparseable value; add an error boundary around money-bearing views.

findings.title: Parser-rejected hostile requests produce no correlated access record
findings.detail: Requests rejected by the HTTP parser (obs-fold, NUL, ANSI bytes - all verified to return 400) never reach the ASGI app, so truelend.access emits nothing for them; only a uvicorn.error line records the rejection, with no request_id and no client address. Probing traffic is therefore the least visible traffic in the log stream.
findings.fix: No change required in this diff - note it for the observability/SIEM story so 4xx parser rejections are ingested and alertable.

refuted.candidate: CR/LF header injection / HTTP response splitting via X-Request-ID
refuted.evidence: Raw-socket probe: llhttp splits the injected bytes into a separate request header (response carried only x-request-id: a); obs-fold/NUL/ANSI variants are rejected with 400 at the parser. Independently, uvicorn httptools_impl.send validates outgoing values against HEADER_VALUE_RE = [\x00-\x08\n-\x1f\x7f] and raises before writing.

refuted.candidate: Log injection - JSON field forgery, extra log lines, ANSI escape injection
refuted.evidence: JSONLogFormatter returns json.dumps(payload) with ensure_ascii=True; the probe value 'x" , "request_id": "spoofed' was emitted as a single escaped string and every captured line parsed as JSON. Control bytes never survive the HTTP parser.

refuted.candidate: Stack trace or internal detail leaked on the 500 path after the pure-ASGI middleware move
refuted.evidence: Live uvicorn: unhandled exception returned 21-byte text/plain 'Internal Server Error' with x-request-id stamped. debug=False, so ServerErrorMiddleware never renders a traceback.

refuted.candidate: PII redaction misses in nested dicts, lists, sets or non-dict payloads
refuted.evidence: The filter scrubs record.getMessage() (the rendered string), so container shape and nesting depth are irrelevant; probe with {'applicant': {'kyc': {'pan': PAN}}, 'docs': [PAN]} produced [REDACTED] in both positions. extra= fields are never emitted at all.

refuted.candidate: Hardcoded secrets, secrets in logs, secrets reachable via the error context
refuted.evidence: Settings declares only service_name and log_level; no credential literal in the diff; no .env/.pem/.key tracked in git.

refuted.candidate: GET /health discloses config, versions, dependency state or secrets
refuted.evidence: Returns the constant {"status":"ok"}; no I/O, no settings read.

refuted.candidate: Backend Money DoS or wrong value via a pathological Decimal exponent
refuted.evidence: 1E+999999999, 1E+9999999999999999999, '9'*200000, NaN, snan, Infinity and 0x1f are all rejected in under 2 ms by the is_finite guard plus quantize's InvalidOperation on the 28-digit context.

Renders {value.format()} as an auto-escaped React text child; no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, raw-HTML prop or template-literal DOM write anywhere in the diff, and format() can only emit digits, comma, dot and minus.
